sentences.text: It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that there were consensual relationship between the petitioner and victim, no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his [2024:RJ-JD:8422] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-1653/2024] incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused- petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material made available to this Court.
5. The victim has been examined under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. during investigation.

I have minutely gone through the statements and the tenor of which suggesting that she was all over a consenting party, eloped with the petitioner at her own free will and volition without there being any compulsion, roamed with him at several places and lived around 14 days in a rented house and at the stage of hearing a bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C., this Court feels that a tentative opinion regarding her being a consenting party can be taken.
The several questions can be raised over the sanctity of the documents showing her date of birth.

If the statement of her father and mother are examined, prima facie, it can be observed that the certificate is not a sacrosanct piece of evidence, she left her father's custody in a surreptitious manner only to join the company of the petitioner.
The FIR has been lodged after three days of her elopement thus, from the circumstances appearing in this case, I see no reason to allow further incarceration of the petitioner allowed.
There is high [2024:RJ-JD:8422] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-1653/2024] probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.
In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
6. It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

7. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 530-Mamta/-
